verdict.rationale: Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol lets merchants cryptographically verify signed agent requests against Visa's public keys and tell credentialed agents apart from anonymous bots. That gives merchants a first-party basis to admit verified agents and turn away unverified ones, and servers can reject replayed or expired signatures. There is no documented merchant-facing control for rate-limiting, or for allow/deny lists covering specific agents or agent platforms. missing for 10: per-agent and per-platform allow/deny policy configuration, rate-limiting controls, documented controls scoped to catalog versus checkout, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a merchant, I can rate-limit, allow, or deny specific agents and agent platforms accessing my catalog and checkout

citations.quote: This allows you to confidently welcome agent-driven commerce while protecting your site from harmful bots.
Instantly distinguish a legitimate, credentialed agent from an anonymous bot.
Servers are able to reject reused or expired signatures, thereby preventing replay attacks.
